A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EmbodiedBench. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 13 models, task and subgoal success rates, ablations, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results, expands the main evaluation to 24 models, and adds navigation input ablations.

M1.justification: The unified planner, action representations, reflection and replanning procedures, prompts, and output schemas are retained. V3 explicitly documents navigation chat-history inputs alongside unchanged baseline scores; this does not establish an underlying algorithm change. The new input variants are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,128 tasks across EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat, EB-Navigation, and EB-Manipulation, with the same capability subsets. The added navigation experiments vary input configurations within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 expand from 13 to 24 models, retaining all original comparators and adding Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Qwen-VL-Max, and variants of InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL, Ovis2, and Gemma-3. Appendix Tables 7–8 also add InternVL2.5-78B-MPO to the step-count comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 adds controlled comparisons of navigation with versus without multimodal chat history and with no, single-target, or multiple detection boxes. The existing temperature, token limit, image resolution, task sample counts, metrics, and environment-step budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G tests chat-history sensitivity across 11 models and all five navigation subsets, distinguishing it from the existing multi-step-image ablation. Appendix F.4 adds a target-only bounding-box experiment. Together these substantially expand navigation diagnostics; earlier ablations, error analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-evaluation run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original scores in Tables 2–3 are retained, but extensive new results are added: Claude-3.7 reaches 67.7% on EB-ALFRED, while InternVL3-78B scores 53.7% on navigation and 26.3% on manipulation. Tables 7–8 add MPO step counts. New Table 10 shows opposing history effects: GPT-4o scores 57.7% with versus 45.3% without chat history, whereas Qwen2-VL-72B scores 21.2% versus 36.3%. These are added comparisons, not improvements to the original method.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the formal interaction-history definition by including the initial observation I0. The POMDP formulation, action definitions, reward, and optimization objective otherwise remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and main conclusions remain: a benchmark spanning action levels and capabilities, a unified agent framework, and evidence of manipulation and long-horizon difficulties with task-dependent reliance on vision. The larger model evaluation expands supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds a specific simulation-only limitation and discusses reproducibility, cost, safety, and real-world applicability. Appendix G hypothesizes that multimodal dialogue training explains model-dependent chat-history effects. Appendix F.4 refines the bounding-box discussion and explains why autonomous object recognition remains the navigation default.

D1.justification: Table 4 supplies identifiers for the added models, and Appendix D adds vLLM to the deployment tools. Section 4.3 and Appendix G clarify navigation chat-history usage. The abstract now explicitly advertises dataset access alongside code; existing prompts, demonstrations, and schemas are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for newer evaluated models, vLLM, real-world robotics, simulation evaluation, and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, while dropping the original Gemini 2023 report. The benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and the substantive positioning against prior benchmarks remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Future Research Directions moves from the main text to Appendix B. V3 adds Limitations and Acknowledgement sections, introduces the chat-history appendix, and makes localized prose and terminology corrections. Most existing paragraphs and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The main result and model-version tables expand, and result tables gain colored headers and average-column shading. V3 adds two navigation comparison tables and Figure 9 illustrating single versus multiple boxes. Existing plots, pipeline illustrations, and case-study figures are retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons and navigation controls make the benchmark more informative, particularly by exposing model-dependent chat-history effects that v1 did not isolate. Clearer input documentation, model identifiers, and simulation-only limitations improve interpretability and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by an introduced reporting error: Section 5.2 attributes manipulation advantages of 14.6 and 5.6 percentage points to Claude-3.5, although Table 3 assigns those advantages to Claude-3.7. The net improvement is useful but limited.
